name: Meiji kosen-ga and aniline-red woodblock print
summary: Early Meiji prints used imported synthetic (aniline) dye in hot reds and purples. Kiyochika's kosen-ga later added Western light and shadow to night scenes of gas lamps, trains and ships.

philosophy.core_thesis: A woodblock print can show the new Japan, with its trains, brick streets and gas light, if it takes the hard colour and the deep shadow of the West.
design_principles: Print the sky in a strong aniline red or violet, with a wiped gradation to blue at the horizon.
Put the light source in the picture: a gas lamp, a window, the sun on water. Let rays and cast shadow fall from it.
Use 4–10 blocks, and let the shadow be a block of dark blue or violet, not a hatched line.
Choose a subject from the new city: a steam train, a brick bank, a steamship, a street at night.
Draw the street in Western perspective with one vanishing point, on a block that a Japanese carver can cut.
Let the red bleed a little at the edge of the area. Do not hold it back.
Print large commercial runs, and keep the outline in thin sumi.
anti_patterns: The pale, soft colour of an Edo print
A flat scene with no light source and no cast shadow
A clean, matt digital vector fill
A neat, restrained red that does not bleed

process.matrix: Cherry-wood blocks, one for each colour and one for the key line.
process.press: No press. A printer rubs the back of the sheet with a baren by hand.
process.image_making: A designer draws, a carver cuts and a printer prints, as in the Edo shop. The subjects are the railway, gas light and the steamship.

inks.strategy: Imported synthetic dyes (aniline) in water, with traditional pigment for the rest. The key block prints first, then the colour blocks in 4–10 passes.

screening.rule: Make a tone with a wiped gradation of 15–50 mm and with flat blocks of dark colour for shadow. The style has no screen.

registration.rule: Allow 0.5–1.0 mm of shift in the large commercial runs. The red may bleed over the edge.

substrate.stock: Thin washi of mulberry fibre, with a cream-brown tone.
substrate.finish: Unsized and absorbent, so the dye sinks in and bleeds a little.

surface.impression: Light. The baren leaves a soft rub on the back.
surface.sheen: Matt. Some of the dyes have a slight shine when fresh.
surface.texture: Flat colour with a soft gradation, a bleed at some edges, and the fibres of thin washi.

marks: Western perspective in a block print

evidence.title: Tokyo kaika meisho
evidence.maker: Nikutei Karyō (presumed Kobayashi Kiyochika) and Kawanabe Kyōsai

emotion.target_response: Hot, strange novelty: the viewer feels a new city that glows red and violet at night.

use_cases: posters on Meiji and railway history
game and film art for a modernising Japan
record sleeves with a hot, night palette
avoid_when: The brief needs a soft, pale Edo look.
The picture needs a photographic tone.

modifiers.how: Keep the light and the shadow. Replace the aniline red with indigo and grey, and tighten the register to 0.2 mm.
Remove the cast shadow and the perspective. Use mineral and plant pigment, and flat colour with a bokashi sky.
